chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Abu Dawud al-Mustarriq, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, three women came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so one of them said, 'My husband does not eat meat,' and the other said, 'My husband does not smell perfume,' and the third said, 'My husband does not approach women.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out dragging his robe until he ascended the pulpit. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'What is the matter with a group of people from my companions who do not eat meat, nor smell perfume, nor approach women?'
Indeed, I eat meat, I smell perfume, and I approach women. So whoever shows preference for my Sunnah, he is from me.

key_terms.يَقْرَبُ: approaches (in the context of marital relations)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) say about companions who abstained from meat, perfume, and marital relations?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s rejection of asceticism (zuhd) that leads to neglecting natural human instincts, specifically citing the abstention from meat, perfume, and marital intimacy. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Prophet’s Sunnah is the balanced middle path, where enjoying permissible pleasures is an act of worship rather than a distraction. The narrative serves as a foundational text for understanding the balance between spiritual devotion and physical well-being in Islamic practice.
